# Documentary proceeds, effective priority and residual supplier obligations

This local `documentary_proceeds_priority` contract distinguishes proceeds assignment from transfer of documentary performance rights. `assign` irrevocably directs proceeds up to a positive cap to one registered recipient. It leaves the exporter responsible for, and entitled to, presenting the document. `transfer_performance` also transfers that right to the recipient; the original exporter can no longer present the transferred document through this service. No transfer, repayment or assignment creates documentary honor before a complying presentation. There is no reversal of an accepted assignment or transfer of performance rights.

Each document has its own assignment cutoff and honor event. A presentation must occur before its honor minute. The current presenter must be the original exporter to use `present`. The actual honor amount is disclosed only at that event and may be lower than face value. If no presentation is made, the honor amount is zero. The stated possible honor amounts are the pre-event information, not guaranteed receipts. A later-maturing document can be presented and assigned within its own still-open deadlines after another document has actually honored.

At honor, allocate actual cash in this order: its recorded senior claim, an effective older transfer on that document, the newly registered assignment up to its cap, then any residual to the exporter's available company cash. Each allocation is limited by the amount then remaining. Earlier claims retain priority even when a later assignment was approved for a larger cap. Recipients need not be the supplier: company and affiliate transfers are legally accepted when authorized. The source document and beneficiary of every actual distribution are recorded.

An older transfer marked revocable can be revoked only at minute 0. Revocation removes that document-funded payment, but accelerates the same lender obligation to an immediate cash payoff. The lender is not forgiven or paid by the revocation itself. New assignments are irrevocable. The customer remains liable for the supplier's residual commercial debt despite any face-value assignment, failure to honor or short distribution. Count actual historical payments and actual supplier distributions; never treat an assignment cap as a payment. The supplier's interim cumulative instalment and final debt may have different deadlines. A positive cash remittance is final and may overpay if the customer fails to reconcile actual receipts.

Unlock `propose_documentary_assignment`.

| Action | Data keys |
| --- | --- |
| `assign` or `transfer_performance` | `record_id`, `recipient_id`, `cap_minor` |
| `present` | `record_id` |
| `revoke_old` | none |
| `pay_lender` | `amount_minor` |
| `pay` | `record_id`, `amount_minor` |

`pay` is for a registered supplier debt or customs bill. `pay_lender` addresses the cash obligation created by revocation; it is unavailable while the existing transfer remains effective. There is no invoice sale, advance, factoring discount, or transfer of supplier performance through a proceeds assignment.

All amounts are integer currency minor units. A logical minute is a business processing window, not elapsed wall-clock time. Read-only queries and preparing or approving requests do not advance time. The owner must approve each exact request before execution. Only successful execution moves money or rights. Actual booking times govern inclusive deadlines.

Each capability takes `case_id`, `action`, and `data`. The tables below list the exact keys allowed inside `data`; unlisted keys are rejected. Record IDs must be obtained through the scoped database search and read tools. Pending outcomes are unknown until their bank event. The customer can explicitly wait for the next actual event. There is no unrecorded outside borrowing, extra operating window, clawback of a final payment, or manual ledger adjustment. Successful execution is idempotent for the same approved request ID.

## Supplier adjustment, actual holder and separate cash authority

The supplier confirmation becomes effective immediately before the first document's honor distribution. It states a genuine commercial credit and the current holder of the remaining supplier claim. The recorded original supplier debt is reduced by that credit; actual earlier payments remain credited. A supplier-claim transfer does not change the exporter's own documentary presentation rights. Payments to the former holder made before the notice's effective event are valid. Payments or documentary distributions to the former holder after the transfer do not discharge the current holder's claim.

The current direct-cash mandate limits the cumulative cash remittances made against the supplier claim during this service. Historical payments outside this service do not consume that mandate. A documentary proceeds assignment uses the separate authority attached to the export document; it does not consume the direct-cash mandate. These are distinct bank authorizations, not interchangeable balances.

`pay_claim` accepts `recipient_id` for a registered supplier-claim recipient and a positive `amount_minor`. It debits available company cash and consumes direct-cash authority. The service accepts either registered claim recipient, but only payment to the holder effective when paid reduces the supplier debt. `pay` with the supplier record is a direct payment to that named supplier under the same cumulative cash mandate. Other `pay` instructions retain their existing meaning for customs and the separately recorded port delivery bill.

The port delivery bill is an independent current obligation. It is not included in the supplier debt, the historical supplier payment, or the creditor notice. No new assignment is required as a service formality: unassigned proceeds still flow to company cash under the original waterfall, and any completion within the actual cash mandate, cash, recipient and timing terms is accepted.

## Standardized exact service interfaces

The following exact interfaces belong to this business service. Unlocking one returns the executable JSON Schema. Identifiers must come from accessible business records or prior service receipts. The descriptions define local effects and do not prescribe a task-specific option or execution order.

### `propose_documentary_assignment`

Prepare a documentary proceeds assignment, performance transfer, presentation, revocation or actual debt payment.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `case_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `action` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
| `data` | object | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.
